reading_decisions.why: I adopt its core separation of the explicit correction field from tool-status inference, but its labels and interpretations claim corrections follow tool outcomes (after failure in E04, after a successful write in E08), which the line order contradicts since every correction sits at L2 before any event.

Its three-way taxonomy and status discipline are useful, but treating failed and unknown episodes as 'requiring correction' is an analyst-imposed definition the corpus never records, and its E08 framing implies correction responding to successful execution even though the correction precedes all events.

It correctly identifies user-initiated redirection of target, scope, or design as the only recorded correction trigger and alone gets E04's correction-before-failure ordering right, though I discount its 'high' confidence and note it never addresses the unknown-status episodes.

output.what_changed_my_view: Checking line order changed my read: every correction is logged at L2, before any tool event, which undercut A's and B's framings of correction as a reaction to success or failure and reframed it as intent realignment. B's broad definition also forced me to separate 'recorded correction' from 'plausibly needs remediation,' a gap the frozen corpus cannot close for failed or unknown episodes.
